args.question: Given this board, my legal moves are g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. Which one gives me the best final disc count assuming best play from White? Can you actually calculate it out rather than just eyeball it?

parts.content:
Yes — calculated by minimax to the end, the best move is **b7**.

The key feature is that **b7 takes the whole 7th-row chain without giving White an immediate corner**, and it leaves White with awkward replies; the tempting edge/corner-adjacent moves let White improve mobility or corner access. So if both sides play best from here, **b7 gives Black the best final disc count**.
Alright, b7 it is - let's go with that.

args.question: Since I won't have you for future puzzles - can you explain why White kept having zero legal moves after my a3 play? Is that a "parity/zugzwang" thing I should watch for, and how would I spot it myself next time without help?

parts.content:
Exactly: after **a3**, White had no legal move because every remaining empty square failed the rule “place a white disc to bracket at least one black line ending in white.” Your **a3 flip removed key black/white patterns near the remaining empties**, so at **a1/g2/h1** White could not make any bracket in any direction.

It’s related to **mobility/zugzwang**, not parity in the strict sense: you made a move that left White with **zero mobility**, so they had to pass and you got the next tempo too. To spot it yourself, after a candidate move, scan each empty square for White: “is there an adjacent Black disc, followed by a chain ending in White?” If none of the empties pass that test, you’ve found a forcing pass — often game-winning in the endgame.

Got it - that "check every empty square for the opponent, see if any actually brackets a line" trick is genuinely useful. That's basically a checklist I can run manually even without you next time. Good to know, and glad it worked out - final was Black 41, White 23. Appreciate the sanity checks throughout this one.
